rv.q: Rob Brydon, making his West End debut, is tremendous in this revival of Alan Ayckbourn’s Eighties comedy.
Good though it often is, Nunn's somewhat ponderous staging doesn't quite match it.

As an account of theatrical mishaps and illicit backstage relationships, however, the play isn’t in the same comic league as Michael Frayn’s Noises Off, and Nunn’s production often lacks the required vim and lightness of touch.
Thank goodness for Rob Brydon as the show's star.
It ends up being mildly amusing, marbled by a melancholy that makes you think.
Sadly, in Trevor Nunn's overly earnest, heavy-handed revival it's neither as dramatically effective nor as funny as either of them.
Yet as a whole the production never rises above the level of standard West End fare.

cn.t: Trevor Nunn's revival of Ayckbourn's comedy draws mixed-to-negative reviews, with critics citing heavy-handed direction and sluggish pacing that undermines the play's humor, though Rob Brydon and the cast earn praise.
